title: latency-cost-fencepost-bench-digest
content:
Purpose:
This note synthesizes a short bench run focused on the "fencepost" effect: small shifts in request size or KV-cache hit behavior that cause outsized changes in tail latency and per-token cost. Goal is to provide a concise reference for product and infra to decide on a short list of knobs to try in the next sprint (slot sizing, prefetch window, and a lightweight quantization policy).

Quick summary (one-paragraph):
Across three representative configs (baseline FP16, quantized INT8 profile Q1, and distilled-small model S1) we observed non-linear step-changes in p95/p99 when request token counts crossed small thresholds (20, 64, 128) — the "fenceposts". INT8 reduced median token-cost by ~27% vs FP16 but made p99 worse by ~12ms in some microburst cases due to slower kernel fallback on edge hardware. Distilled S1 yields the best p99 stability for tiny requests (<30 tokens) at a modest quality loss; cost per 1k tokens for S1 is ~45% lower than FP16 for the same conversational mix.

Experimental setup:
- Hardware: mixed fleet used in lab: 2 x A100-80GB baseline hosts (core), 4 x A10 edge hosts (edge).
- Model variants:
  * FP16-baseline: rwi/gpt-13b-fp16 (canonical serving build)
  * Q1-int8: rwi/gpt-13b-int8 (profile Q1 quant settings, per-layer scale)
  * S1-distill: rwi/gpt-6b-distill (half params, same tokenizer)
- Workloads: sessionized chat traces sampled from production dev traffic (100k sessions, stratified by average request tokens: tiny <30, short 30-90, medium 90-300).
- Metrics captured: p50/p95/p99 generation latency (ms), end-to-end request latency (ms), tokens/sec (throughput), and $/1k tokens estimated from infra costing model.
- Run mode: steady-state bursts (sustained QPS with injected microbursts), and cold-warm start mix (10% cold).

Key numeric findings (aggregate):
- Median generation latency (ms): FP16 42, INT8 31, S1 18
- p95 generation latency (ms): FP16 84, INT8 92, S1 36
- p99 generation latency (ms): FP16 162, INT8 174, S1 78
- End-to-end request p99 (includes network + mux): FP16 230, INT8 248, S1 120
- Throughput (tokens/sec per GPU host): FP16 3,400, INT8 4,200, S1 7,100
- Cost per 1k tokens (dollars): FP16 $0.045, INT8 $0.033, S1 $0.025

ASCII visual: latency vs token-count fenceposts (p95)

Token bucket:    <30      30-64     65-127    128+
FP16 p95 (ms):   52       78        120       200
INT8 p95 (ms):   48       88        140       210
S1 p95 (ms):     28       34        60        110

Observation: p95 jumps are concentrated at 64 and 128 boundaries; S1 smooths those jumps considerably. INT8 shows an intermediate pattern but exhibits a secondary penalty at the 65-127 bucket on A10 hosts.

Microburst trace excerpt (illustrative):
- workload: 1k concurrent tiny sessions (avg 18 tokens) injected for 20s
- FP16 p99 delta during burst: +42ms from baseline
- INT8 p99 delta during burst: +58ms from baseline
- S1 p99 delta during burst: +14ms from baseline

Why does INT8 sometimes hurt p99? (notes & hypotheses)
- Kernel path variability: INT8 profile uses a fast fused kernel for most layers but falls back to a slower generic kernel for long-sequence edge cases. On A10 hosts the fallback decision has higher jitter (measured internal traces show kernel-switch events clustered around fenceposts).
- Memory/workspace pressure: quantized runtime increases temporary workspace usage in the allocator pattern we use; when many tiny sessions are multiplexed this can cause transient contention and queueing.
- Incompatibility with current prefetch window: our prefetch heuristic assumes FP16 per-layer timing; with INT8 the prefetch size occasionally underestimates needed KV cache warmup, causing repeated short decoding stalls.

Cost vs SLA tradeoff table (rounded):
- Objective: choose a config for latency-sensitive tiny-interaction product (p95 <= 60ms, p99 <= 150ms) with <$0.03/1k tokens target.

Option A: FP16 baseline
- p95: typically OK for short requests but p99 hotspots at fenceposts; cost too high ($0.045).
Option B: INT8 (Q1)
- Cost: meets $0.03 target on throughput, but p99 breaches goal during microbursts on edge hardware without scheduler tweaks.
Option C: Distilled S1
- Cost: comfortably under target and p99 safe; quality tradeoff needs embedding-level eval but for tiny requests quality degradation is modest in our manual checks.

Recommendations (short list for next 2 sprints):
1) Quick wins (1 week):
   - Add a fencepost-aware admission control: cap slot packing to avoid mixing >X tiny sessions with medium sessions on same GPU. Implement as a simple token-count bucket in the scheduler.
   - Adjust prefetch window for INT8 profile: increase prefetch multiplier for token counts near fenceposts (30-140) and measure.
2) Medium (2-4 weeks):
   - Kernel-warmup probe: add a micro-probing step during warmup to detect likely kernel-fallback cases and prefer hosts with consistent fused-kernel paths for INT8 traffic.
   - Nightly quality-run for S1: automated eval with 200 prompt set to measure delta in ROUGE/embedding-sim for the tiny-interaction cohort.
3) Longer (quarter):
   - Investigate allocator changes to reduce workspace jitter for quantized workload under high multiplexing.
   - Consider hybrid routing: tiny sessions -> S1 on edge; long sessions -> FP16 or INT8 on core, with transparent pricing.

Open questions / unresolved: 
- How representative are the sampled traces for international regions (APAC)? We observed slightly worse INT8 jitter in APAC (A10-equivalent hosts) but we need region-specific runs.
- The cost model used assumes stable price parity across fleet; procurement changes (spot vs reserved) will alter $/1k tokens materially.
- Quality delta for S1 on long-sessions (>300 tokens) is unknown; we need an explicit eval for the long tail.

Appendix A — lightweight ascii sparkline (p99 per-config over token-size):
Token-size -> 0----30----60----90----120----150----300----600
FP16 p99   : |===|------|========|===========|===============|
INT8 p99    : |==|--------|===========|=============|================|
S1 p99      : |-|--|----|------|----|-----|---------|
(visual: S1 compressed, FP16 and INT8 have stepped growth at 64/128)

Appendix B — links to experiment artifacts:
- Raw trace bundle (GCS): gs://redwood-bench/latency-fencepost/2029-06-04/ (internal)
- Analysis notebook: https://github.com/redwood-inference/benchmarks/blob/main/fencepost/analysis.ipynb

TL;DR: If we need the cheapest, safest short-term pick for tiny interactive features, S1-distill is the lowest-risk path right now; INT8 is attractive for steady-state throughput and cost but requires scheduler and prefetch mitigations to avoid p99 regressions in microburst scenarios.

Notes to self / TODO:
- Run region-specific (EU/APAC) microburst sequences with same configs (assigned to Marco).
- Post a short summary to #infra-bench with a one-slide ascii table.
- Open a small spike PR to try prefetch multiplier tweak (Leah).

End of digest.
